newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY AUGUST PSBR SEEN AT JUST 2.0 TRLN LIRE.
newsitem.headline: ITALY AUGUST PSBR SEEN AT JUST 2.0 TRLN LIRE.

text.p: Italy's August state sector borrowing requirement is expected to be around 2.0 trillion lire, well below the 8.47 trillion needed in August 1996, analysts said.
This would take the cumulative deficit for the first eight months of the year to 31.75 trillion lire, some 40 trillion less than that in the same period last year.

Analysts told Reuters the August data should keep Italy on track to meet its goal of a public administration deficit of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product this year, as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to sign up to the planned single European currency from its 1999 launch.
They attributed the sharp drop in August in large part to a first tranche of some 5.0 trillion lire in tax on employees' severance pay paid by companies into the state coffers.
Also helping was tight government control on treasury drawings by local authorities and extra revenue still coming in from this year's one-off Eurotax on incomes.
Italy's borrowing requirement in July was 4.3 trillion lire, some 5.5 trillion lire less than the same month last year.

Economists are already looking ahead to the September-December period, "a crucial time due to budgetary effects and to test the government's ability to continue to hold down spending," said Lorenzo Codogno of Bank of America.

"July and August are important months for boosting the recovery in public accounts because it's more difficult in autumn which is seasonally a more rigid spending period," added Cosimo Musiello of Prometeia.
